statement.text:
Let $p$ be a prime number. A group $\Gamma$ is called $p$-Jordan if there exist constants $J$ and $e$ such that any finite subgroup $G\subset\Gamma$ contains a normal abelian subgroup of order coprime to $p$ and of index at most $J\cdot |G(p)|^e$. (For example by the results of Brauer--Feit and Larsen--Pink, for any field $K$ of characteristic $p$ the group $\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$ is $p$-Jordan with $e=3$.) Let the $p$-Jordan exponent $e(\Gamma)$ of the group $\Gamma$ be the infimum of all constants $e$ for which the above bound holds for some constant $J=J(e)$.

a) Is it true that this infimum is always attained?

b) Is it true that $e(\Gamma)\leqslant 3$ for any $p$-Jordan group $\Gamma$?
